narration: Touch the table. It feels completely solid. But zoom far enough in, and touch stops looking like two hard surfaces meeting. Atoms in your fingertip and the table carry diffuse electron distributions. Push them close and electrical interactions resist further compression, while quantum rules including Pauli exclusion make crowding the electrons into the same states energetically costly. Your fingertip deforms by a microscopic amount. Nerves detect that resistance, and your brain calls it touch. So contact is real at our scale — underneath, it is matter resisting matter.
captions: TOUCH THE TABLE. NOW ZOOM IN.
THAT RESISTANCE IS WHAT YOU FEEL.
